title: DREO Space Heater Review: 3 Weeks of Testing in My Home Office
metaDescription: Tested the DREO 1500W space heater for 3 weeks in my office. Here's what I found about heating speed, noise levels, and energy efficiency.
content:
## Setup took about five minutes straight out of the box

No assembly required - just plug it in and you're ready to go. The remote comes with batteries already installed, which is a nice touch. The unit feels solid when you pick it up, heavier than it looks at first glance.

## Heating Performance in Real Use

This thing heats up my 120 square foot office faster than my old baseboard heater ever did. Within about two minutes, I can feel the warmth spreading across the room. The PTC ceramic element seems to distribute heat more evenly compared to traditional coil heaters I've used before.

The 70-degree oscillation feature works well for covering more area. Instead of having one super hot spot directly in front of the heater, the rotating function spreads warmth throughout the space. I keep it positioned in the corner and it reaches my desk about eight feet away without any issues.

Tested it during some particularly cold mornings when my main heating wasn't keeping up. The thermostat function maintains a consistent temperature once it reaches your setting. I usually keep mine set around 72 degrees and it cycles on and off as needed.

## Noise Levels and Daily Use

Running this heater while on video calls hasn't been a problem. It's quieter than my laptop fan when it's working hard. There's a slight hum when the fan kicks in, but nothing that interferes with conversation or concentration.

The different speed settings let you balance heating power with noise. On the lowest setting, it's nearly silent but takes longer to warm the room. Medium setting hits the sweet spot for me - good heating without being distracting.

## Energy Usage Observations

Using this instead of heating my entire house during work hours seems to make a difference on my electric bill. The 1500W max power draw is typical for space heaters this size, but the thermostat control means it's not running constantly like some cheaper models.

The eco mode reduces power consumption when the target temperature is reached. I can't give you exact numbers, but I've noticed it cycling off more frequently than staying on, which should help with efficiency.

## Remote and Controls

The remote is responsive from across the room. All the main functions are accessible - temperature, timer, oscillation, and power modes. The display on the unit shows current temperature and settings clearly.

Timer function works up to 12 hours, which is handy for overnight use or setting it to warm up the room before you arrive. The buttons on the unit itself are straightforward if you misplace the remote.

## Safety Features in Practice

The tip-over protection activated when I accidentally knocked it over while moving furniture. It immediately shut off and wouldn't restart until I set it upright again. The overheat protection hasn't been needed, but it's reassuring to know it's there.

The exterior stays relatively cool to the touch even after running for hours. The front grille gets warm but not burning hot like some heaters I've owned.

## What Could Be Better

The power cord could be longer - it's about six feet, which limits placement options in some rooms. Extension cords work but aren't ideal for high-wattage appliances.

The oscillation makes a slight clicking sound at each direction change. It's not loud, but you notice it in a quiet room. The clicking happens every few seconds during oscillation mode.

Wish it had a more gradual temperature adjustment. The thermostat jumps in larger increments rather than precise degree-by-degree control.
pros: Heats rooms quickly with PTC ceramic technology
Operates quietly enough for work calls and sleeping
Remote control works well from across the room
Safety features including tip-over and overheat protection
Eco mode helps reduce energy consumption when target temp is reached
cons: Power cord is only about 6 feet long, limiting placement options
Oscillation mechanism makes slight clicking sounds during operation
Thermostat adjustments aren't precise - jumps in larger temperature increments
Heavier than expected, making it less portable for frequent moving
verdict: This heater delivers solid performance for office and bedroom use with good safety features and quiet operation. While it has some minor drawbacks like cord length and clicking sounds, it heats efficiently and the thermostat control works reliably for maintaining comfortable temperatures.
targetAudience: People working from home who need efficient heating for single rooms, anyone wanting a quiet heater for bedrooms, and those looking to reduce heating costs by warming specific spaces instead of entire homes
